services.name: SDI Estimating Intelligence
services.requires: Runs on the engine host — started from the command line, not from here.
services.desc: Deterministic cost-estimating engine — SolidWorks PDF/DXF in, costed workbook out.
services.detail:
Live cost-estimating engine that mirrors the SDI estimating workbook to the cell. All 80 workbook formulas reverse-engineered. A growing RAG store of historical SDI jobs feeds comparables on material, labour and operations. Five-tier price chain with source attribution and confidence on every line — no priceless rows. Cell-level parity report against the manually completed workbook. In a five-jobs-a-week parallel run with James Ryan and Dave’s estimating team — Tim, Howard and Tony — ahead of a targeted GO-LIVE in September / October 2026, decided on the reviews that come back. Eleven jobs have run in the past two weeks and six more run this week. Feedback is back from all three estimators — Howard on two jobs, Tony on one, Tim on three — and every point has gone into the engine as a rule that carries to every job: a change register of numbered decisions (D-016 to D-078) records who ruled it, on which job, whether it is generic or a scoped pilot, where it is implemented and the test that proves it. Where the engine and an estimator still differ, the line says so and names who is asked.
Landed since 27 Aug 2026.
  • The finished estimate is e-mailed automatically to a saved recipients list the moment a run completes — workbook, report and covering note. The customer quote is withheld while an estimate is provisional.
  • An AI Explanation tab in the workbook, the same text as section 14 of the job report and the covering e-mail: every material block and labour row reconciled to the sheet’s own totals, labour split into set-up and run with the figure at 1 to 250 off, and the lines that still need a person listed worst-first with the money at stake.
  • Parity from the portal — the harness was rebuilt to measure the estimate rather than its own parser, and runs on every job with a manual sheet attached, filing a ledger row per job.
  • One estimate at every quantity asked for (1, 50, 100, 250, 500), one workbook per quantity, with order-level freight divided per unit rather than a pallet landed on each.
  • A run is measured — every phase timed, memory and CPU sampled during a live estimate. Those figures sized the shared workstation.
Landed 7 Sep 2026.
  • One record behind every document — the workbook tabs, the covering e-mail, the job report and the quote all read one costed record built after the sheet calculates, so money, sources, gaps, decisions, finish and release status are the same on all four. The job report is now the estimator’s page: unit cost and release status, then the decisions still open with the money riding on each, then the BOM under its assemblies and the priced route; the diagnostics collapsed beneath.
  • The workbook is five tabs, not nine — the estimators’ own three, then AI Explanation (decisions first) and AI Provenance (value used → source → evidence → estimator action; the BOM hierarchy; the route decision by decision; identity through the pack).
After the parallel run — the automated pipeline, and on demand. The parts exist as separate controls on the estimating page; the next step joins them into one run and keeps each available on its own.
  • One button imports the full and latest drawing pack from Document Manager into staging — latest revision by the data inside the file. Next
  • One click generates the estimate with its explains and e-mails it with the client quote. Next
  • Parity at the time of the run where a manual sheet exists, or added afterwards where the AI run comes first. Partly in
  • Amend the estimate, then generate the quote from the estimator’s own figure. In
  • Print the PDFs and DXFs of a pack from the portal. In
  • Beyond, no timetable: China quotations (buttons in, analytics to follow) and multi-PDF packs (working, needs testing; runs against our model or purely against an LLM).

services.name: SDI Technical Design Intelligence
services.status: In build · P2 hardening · P3.1 started
services.desc: Reads SolidWorks project data natively, and builds SDI its own PDM — Sept 2026 to Feb 2027.
services.detail:
Two threads run under one workstream. The Document Manager API tools (P1, P2) pull the correct drawing pack for a project straight into the estimating app and into the shop-floor Production folder — reading without a SolidWorks seat, read-only, never writing to the live CAD share. Then an SDI in-house PDM (P3.1–P3.4) gives engineering trustworthy file management, CAD-awareness, revision control and release workflows. It is built on GitLab + LFS with a DM API intelligence layer over PostgreSQL — it is not an integration with the SOLIDWORKS PDM vault.
Proven, and the seat is now installed. Four SolidWorks COM tools are POC-complete and demoed to Ed Cooper and Ian B — C1 multi-format export (including DXF flat patterns), C2 the topple / weight / interference / hole-alignment check suite, C3 drawing generation from a model, C4 machine-tolerance validation against the TRUMPF tool list (in progress). Every one carried go-live subject to SolidWorks licence, and a permanent seat is now installed on the estimating laptop — so all four can run there, among them the DXF generation that answers the estimating engine’s largest accuracy limiter. Seats on the other machines are the remaining question.
Week to 11 Sep 2026 (Yogesh’s report). P2 hardening after the 2 Sep approval: the two checkouts untangled (UAT on 8000, feature branch on 8001); the licence key and password-less e-mail fixed; the fifteen missing BOM previews diagnosed — twelve were library hardware pointing at a folder that did not exist, repointed and verified, three are sheet-metal parts to be re-saved in SolidWorks; the project-10975 crash traced to stale SolidWorks lock files opened as assemblies. P2 gained extraction history, diagnostics and a metrics endpoint, live mismatch alerts in Step 4 with recorded acknowledgement, and richer e-mail notifications; tests went from about 240 to 363. Six short demo videos with write-ups cover the SolidWorks COM API, the file-extraction endpoint, the DM API proof of concept and P2 itself. The design meeting with Ian B and Ed Cooper set the next actions: ISO release traceability, overwrite behaviour on re-run, an isometric preview for the estimating quote page, a “promote drawing files” button, and staging for self-service testing. P2 keeps 29 Sep with the feature branch merging to main w/c 21 Sep; P3.1 has started, Ubuntu and Docker installed for the PDM MVP.
Why the dates run to February. Yogesh is the sole developer. Requirement collection, development, unit testing, peer review, deployment and go-live are all hands-on and must run one at a time — only user testing overlaps. That, plus leave from 10 Dec 2026 to 4 Jan 2027, is what pushes P3.3 and P3.4 into the new year. Re-based on 4 Sep 2026: each tool’s deployment days are now carved out of the next build, which moved P2 and the PDM phases right by one to three weeks. The dates are a capacity constraint, not an estimate of effort.
Week of 4 Sep 2026. P2 demoed at the technical design meeting on 2 Sep (Ian B, Ed Cooper) and approved, with the name confirmed as Production Design Extraction. Landed: primary/supplementary assembly roles; a DWG/PDF revision-mismatch rule with severity-based alerts, surveyed across 297 Boots projects (436 matched pairs, 34 split); the OneDrive/toolbox missing-file problem solved via configured read-only roots (980 filenames indexed, 10 of 11 missing 11650 parts resolving); an audit log, a drive-health chip and a Step 5 shop-floor e-mail option. The P3 Design Vault feasibility is complete. Watch-points: network-scan speed over Wi-Fi, and the Vault POC needs a Linux/GitLab machine by 10 Sep — the shared workstation.

services.name: SDI Drawing Search Intelligence
services.desc: Find the fixture that already exists before anybody draws a new one.
services.detail:
Drawing search for the design and technical teams — the project the delivery tracker calls the Fixture Library. Live, out of UAT, on 32,422 indexed drawings: search by what is actually printed on the sheet — the client, the material, the finish, the RAL, the job number, a line from a note — and open the SolidWorks or 3ds Max file straight from the result. SDI has drawn the same bracket, the same shelf and the same plinth many times over, and until now the only index of that was what a designer happened to remember.
Where it is
Live. UAT with the studio designers ran from Monday 7 Sep 2026 and it is out of UAT ahead of the ~25 Sep 2026 tracker date. Ian tested it and liked it, which is why it went in. It is on this portal’s menu as SDI Drawing Search Intelligence, directly below its user guide, and opens in a new tab at http://LC-328802:5000/. This week’s fixes came from watching real use: opening the right drawing, and not hiding drawings filed in unusual places — this year’s Boots Dynamix drawings were not showing at all and now are. The index grows as drawings are filed. The user guide is published on this portal as the SDI Drawing Search Intelligence Guide. Muhammad keeps this project through UAT and go-live while moving, from September, onto the business analysis for SDI Manufacturing Intelligence: mapping the live production spreadsheet for BOMs and routes for the warehouse, so that process can be automated and understood on the way into Sage X3, and mapping the design DXF process onto CNC machining — documented as a BRD and user stories, planned and executed with James Gray. Client Briefing, his other project, was held from 4 Sep and is back on the agenda from 16 Sep.
What decides its value now. It went live before the 25 Sep 2026 date it was tracking, so the build overlaps listed on 4 Sep did not bite. The measure from here is designers using it on real jobs: the fixes come from watching real use, and a drawing filed in an unusual place is a bug to fix, not a limitation to accept. Next: more designers on it.
What this is not. It is not the estimating engine’s description matching pointed at a different table. That scores word overlap between two pieces of text; this searches the IMAGES, which is why it can find a fixture whose description never said what it looked like. The two may meet later — a drawing found here has a part code, and that code is a key the price chain already understands — but they are separate pieces of work today.

services.name: SDI Client Briefing Intelligence
services.desc: A client brief comes back structured and with precedent attached, not with a blank sheet. Held 4 Sep; back on the agenda, Muhammad working on it.
services.detail:
The client-facing project on the same tracker, where it is called Client Briefing. A brief is captured and turned into something structured, and that structure is run against what SDI has already built so the response carries precedent: the fixtures, the drawings, and the jobs they were made for. Approved by Stuart and Bec, and scoped around a large job of Stuart’s that needs its requirements settled in detail before any of it is built.
Where it is
Back on the agenda from 16 Sep 2026. Held from 4 Sep 2026 with requirements gathering stopped at 25%; Muhammad has resumed it. It takes a brief however it arrives — e-mail, a recorded call, a WhatsApp voice note — and turns it into one consistent brief: which of the four teams it belongs to, what can be filled in from what SDI already knows about the account, and what is still missing, with the gaps that block work separated from those that can follow. It never books anything itself; every brief goes to Jonathan to approve. Honestly early: two briefs through it, both Muhammad’s own, none yet on live work. What it needs is time with Jonathan and real briefs. Muhammad carries it alongside the business analysis for the Manufacturing / CNC SDI Intelligence automations.
What already exists
It is not restarting from a blank page. A web template is already developed and is being enhanced rather than designed. An e-mail AI agent analyses client communications, which is what lets a brief arrive as an e-mail, a recorded call or a WhatsApp voice note and still come back structured. Design and account manager details are collated against the brief, so the right people and the account’s own history travel with it. The purpose, stated plainly, is to promote communication and collaboration across the four teams: one consistent brief, the gaps named, and nothing booked without Jonathan’s approval.
The tracker’s dates are not re-claimed. Its plan — scope sign-off 21 Sep, build 25 Sep to 15 Oct, testing and UAT through October, release ~Nov 2026 — is kept for the record. The project is back on, but no date is claimed until Jonathan has run real briefs through it.
How this differs from SDI Brief & Concept Intelligence, listed below: that one takes a brief and generates something NEW — renders, concepts, parametric 3D. This one takes a brief and finds what ALREADY EXISTS. A client asking for something SDI has built before should be shown it rather than sold a concept render of it.

services.name: SDI Sage X3 Data Migration
services.desc: Every table in SDI Live given a disposition, and the ones that matter loaded into Sage X3 before the ERP goes live.
services.detail:
The Access database behind SDI Live is being moved to Sage X3. Eleven X3 templates are covered by built extract views drawing on eighteen core source tables; everything else in the database — and the Crystal Reports layer sitting on top of it — needs a stated disposition even where that disposition is “not migrated”. This page is the consolidated view: what is mapped, what every other table does, what the data quality actually is, and the three weeks that get it loaded.
Two dates, and they do not conflict. All data in X3 by Friday 30 October 2026. The ERP itself goes live 4 January 2027, which is the date on the programme timeline and is not SDI Intelligence’s to move. The migration finishes first on purpose, so the business is loading a system it has already proved rather than proving one during cutover.
Where these figures come from. The row counts and the table dispositions are the SDI Live extract and the analysis run against it — not anything this portal computes. Where a number is derived or approximate the table says so, and the three things that are not yet known are listed at the foot of this page rather than filled in with a guess.

sections.title: 5 · What has to hold for the date to hold
sections.body:
End of October is achievable, and only if three things hold.Two of them do not hold today, so this is a target with a gate rather than a commitment.

  1. The three third-party items must clear in week 1. The sign convention blocks the final AR and AP extracts, and without non-production access and the product-category confirmation the trial load cannot run in week 3.
  2. Cleansing is real work, not sign-off. 20,724 blank descriptions and the blank sales-order-status decision are record-level effort for the business owners. Three weeks is tight at that volume.
  3. Only one trial-load cycle fits. The original plan had two trial loads plus a dress rehearsal; compressing to a single load, fix and rehearse pass removes the safety net, so any structural surprise moves the date.
The gate, and the recommendation. Treat 30 October as thetarget and put an explicit decision point at the end of week 1: if the three third-partyitems are not confirmed by Friday 16 October, the date rebaselines to mid-November. Thatprotects against a failed cutover rather than a slipped date, which is the more expensive ofthe two by a distance.

sections.title: 6 · What is not yet known
sections.body:
Three things are genuinely not known yet, and each is a line in theplan above rather than an assumption baked into it.

  • The Crystal Reports inventory does not exist. These are .rpt files rather than tables, so they were never in the table dump and nothing about them can be stated from it. The register on this page is a placeholder until the filenames, the reports menu export or the folder listing are captured. Due by end of October, opened in week one.
  • The UDEF family has not been analysed. Some of those tables are custom fields bolted onto live records and must land in X3 user fields; others are staging and drop. Deciding without the column definitions would be guessing, so the column-definition query is a week-one task and the decision is field by field.
  • Routings and works orders: in scope or still parked? They are not among the eleven templates — works-order routings were parked earlier. If they are now wanted for the October go-live that is a scope addition, and it changes both the ASC disposition list above and the load waves in week three. This one needs an answer before the plan is final.

inputs: The SDI Live Access database (Access Supply Chain) — ~300 tables
The eleven built X3 extract views
Historical pricing, supplier master and BOM data
Business owner sign-off per data area
outputs: A disposition for every source table
A cleansing action list per owner
A reports register: rebuild or retire
services.phase: ERP programme · data migration owned by SDI · all data by 30 OCT 2026
services.invoke: Nothing to run. This is the plan of record: the consolidated table disposition, the cleansing actions by owner, and the three weeks to cutover. The workbook that carries the same content line by line — tasks, owners, dependencies and a RAG status per row — is the next artefact.
services.next: The week-one gate. If the sign convention, the non-production environment and the product-category confirmation are not settled by Friday 16 October, the date rebaselines to mid-November rather than being defended into a failed cutover. Before that: the answer on routings, the UDEF column-definition query, and the Crystal Reports inventory opened. Then the price seam: from the ERP go-live the estimating engine reads its material and supplier prices from X3 rather than from SDI Live, so the versioned price and supplier seam — and a dual-running validation across the changeover — is the piece of this that lands back on the engine.

services.name: SDI Design for Manufacture Intelligence
services.desc: Every design AI-reviewed before the shop floor — flags cost, suggests alternatives, auto-BOM.
services.detail:
AI review of every design before manufacture. Flags costly features with a £ impact estimate. Suggests redesign alternatives. Auto-generates flat patterns, bend sequences, weld sequences and full BOM. The BOM feeds straight into the estimating engine — closing the loop between design and estimate.
Part of this is already proven, not planned. The SolidWorks COM POC (Yogesh Kumar, complete mid-Aug 2026) already performs several of the checks this service was scoped to need:
  • interference-check — clash detection, exiting non-zero so it can gate a build rather than only reporting
  • hole-alignment-check — cross-component hole-axis alignment. There is no SolidWorks API for this; it reads cylindrical-face geometry directly and flags near-misses
  • topple-analysis — tip-over stability from centre of mass and support footprint, measured at ~25.9° on 12173-02-GA
  • weight-check — mass against a limit
  • machine / standards validation — in progress, against the TRUMPF tool list and SDI design standards. This is the DFM rules engine in all but name
And export-dxf and export-package generate the flat patterns, STEP and IGES this service was going to have to build. So the remaining work is narrower than the phase suggests: the £ impact per feature, the redesign suggestions, and wiring the generated BOM into the estimating engine. The geometry checks exist.
outputs: DFM flag report (£ impact per feature)
services.phase: Phase 3 · Q4 2026 — geometry checks already proven
services.invoke: Partly built. The COM POC covers the geometry and export side; what remains is the cost model per feature and the BOM handoff into estimating. services.name: SDI Voice CRM Intelligence · Sandbox Pilot
services.desc: Morning outbound call updates Nick’s NG project records by voice — read back, confirmed, audited.
services.detail: The first concrete voice pilot, requested by Nick Garrish (Account Director). Between 08:30 and 09:30 the system calls Nick, reads out his highest-priority or most out-of-date projects, takes the updates by voice, reads each proposed change back for explicit confirmation, and only then writes it to a SharePoint sandbox List. Every change is journalled (old value, new value, time, user, source) and a daily summary is emailed. A custom Azure application is the workflow owner — Microsoft Graph is the data path into Microsoft 365, not the application, and the speech/AI layer never writes records directly. Scope is deliberately narrow: the sandbox List only, records whose AM Owner is exactly NG, and the live project tracker in Teams is untouched until testing is approved.

sections.title: Microsoft Graph
sections.body: Reads and updates the selected SharePoint sandbox List. Access is granted to the application explicitly (selected-permissions consent) — no live-tracker permission is requested. No additional licence beyond the existing Microsoft 365 access.

sections.title: Azure Communication Services
sections.body: Places and controls the outbound telephone call — dialling Nick’s mobile, playing prompts, receiving voice input, raising call events. ACS provides the telephone connection only; the conversation and all business logic sit in the application.

sections.title: Speech and AI
sections.body: Azure AI Speech for listening and speaking, and an Azure-hosted language model for interpretation. This layer interprets and responds — it makes no record writes of its own.

sections.title: Custom Azure application
sections.body: Python or C#, hosted in Azure. Schedules the call and selects the authorised NG projects, co-ordinates telephony + speech + AI, validates proposed changes, reads them back and obtains explicit confirmation, writes through Graph handling concurrent edits and retries safely, records the audit trail, co-ordinates report refreshes and sends the daily summary.

sections.title: SharePoint List
sections.body: Structured sandbox records with required unique Project IDs, owner identity, status and next actions — defined fields, per-record forms, status views and version history. Use status views rather than moving or deleting records. Excel is retained as a reporting output, not the system of record.

sections.title: Scheduling
sections.body: An Azure timer or Power Automate — use one scheduler, not both. Premium licensing is not required for the pilot: the Azure application schedules the calls and performs the updates directly. Assess Premium only if a selected flow genuinely requires it.

sections.title: Audit and monitoring
sections.body: Pending and completed updates are recorded durably so a retry can never repeat a saved change. Failed writes, audit steps or report refreshes report their actual outcome — never a false “complete”. Raw call recording is not required by default.

sections.title: Approval and boundaries
sections.body: IT and the SharePoint owner approve the sandbox, restrict human and application access, and enable version history. The application re-checks the NG owner and the record version at every update — a filtered view alone is not security. Nick is authenticated before any confidential project detail is read out.

sections.title: Sage X3 — later, separate approval
sections.body: A separate service using Sage-supported interfaces, read-only initially (customer code, order status, invoiced value). Field ownership and stable ID mappings to be agreed with the X3 team ahead of the 4 January go-live. Tracker completion or hold status must never automatically close or alter an ERP order; live writeback requires a separately approved scope.

sections.title: Not required for the pilot
sections.body: Copilot Studio voice capabilities and Office Scripts. Office Scripts are not needed for List updates and should not be assumed to refresh every workbook connection or pivot table — consider them only for specific Excel reporting tasks.

sections.title: Indicative running cost
sections.body: One user, a 10–15 minute call on roughly 22 working days a month: an initial £50–£150 per month Azure operating allowance covers consumption-based voice, AI and application hosting. IT to confirm the selected services and tariffs before approval.

inputs: SharePoint sandbox List records (AM Owner = NG)
Sage X3 customer / order data (later, read-only)
outputs: Confirmed record updates in the sandbox List
Update journal (old / new value, confirmation, outcome)
Refreshed sandbox reporting (Excel or Power BI)
Daily email — saved changes, failed changes, outstanding actions

services.name: SDI Web Intelligence
services.desc: Layered AI-readiness on the existing WordPress site — not a rewrite.
services.detail: WordPress is the right engine for what SDI is doing — AI search engines love it for clean HTML, schema/JSON-LD support and B2B-intel integrations. Rather than rewrite the site, we layer six AI-native upgrades on top, and use this portal to mock new sections privately before they touch the staging WordPress clone.

sections.title: 1 · LinkedIn → site insights feed
sections.body: Publish once on LinkedIn, syndicate automatically to a News / Insights section on wearesdi.com so AI crawlers see fresh SDI activity immediately. Tools: Elfsight feed widget or Jetpack Social with a filter on the relevant topics.

sections.title: 2 · AI-native SEO & content
sections.body: Adopt an AI SEO plugin — Rank Math with Content AI, or AIOSEO. These optimise for the technical vocabulary engineers and procurement people actually search, so SDI ranks for the high-intent, long-tail prompts AI search engines surface.

sections.title: 3 · RAG chatbot on site
sections.body: A retrieval-augmented chatbot (e.g. MxChat) trained on SDI’s own technical docs and case studies. Acts as a 24/7 technical sales assistant or "AI product expert" — not a generic FAQ bot. Same RAG pattern already running in the estimating engine.

sections.title: 4 · GA4 + B2B visitor identification
sections.body: GA4 wired to Sage X3 (when ready). Layer a B2B visitor-ID tool on top to surface which companies read which pages. Dealfront (Leadfeeder + Echobot, EU-built, GDPR-aligned) is the recommended path for the UK — Clearbit folded into HubSpot’s Breeze Intelligence and is no longer a standalone option. Albacross is an alternative. Track stakeholder journeys (multiple visitors from one prospect company) and conversion attribution back to the originating content.

sections.title: 5 · Predictive next-best content
sections.body: AI suggests the most relevant follow-up content to each visitor based on the current page — e.g. a Vue case study automatically surfaced when someone reads the cinema-display capability page. Lifts engagement and quote-request conversion.

sections.title: 6 · Multimodal search optimisation
sections.body: Tag SDI’s video and high-res facility imagery with ImageObject / VideoObject schema so AI tools can "see" the facility and processes, not just read text. Alt text, captions, transcripts — all built for AI ingestion as well as accessibility.

services.name: SDI Recording Intelligence · OBS
services.desc: Professional screen recording and live streaming — AI demos, presentations, facility content and virtual camera for Teams.
services.detail: OBS (Open Broadcaster Software) is the capture and broadcast layer at SDI. Record AI tool demos, estimating engine runs, design presentations and facility walkthroughs for the portal, SEEN content and client materials. Free, open source, runs locally. Download from obsproject.com if not already installed.

sections.title: First-time setup
sections.body:
Settings → Video: Base Resolution 1920×1080, Output 1920×1080, FPS 30. Settings → Output → Recording: set a recordings folder (e.g. C:\SDIRecordings). Settings → Audio: Desktop Audio = your speakers; Mic = your microphone.

Do not record straight to plain MP4. An MP4 is only finalised when recording stops cleanly — a crash, a power loss or a flat battery leaves an unplayable file with the whole recording lost. Record to MKV (or hybrid MP4 if your OBS offers it) and use File → Remux Recordings to produce an MP4 afterwards; remuxing is a container swap, it takes seconds and re-encodes nothing. This matters here because an engine run can last two hours.

Encoder: NVENC on an NVIDIA GPU, Intel QuickSync (QSV) on an Intel Core Ultra machine — which is what the estimating laptop is, so NVENC will not be offered there. x264 is the fallback and the only one that costs real CPU, which is worth avoiding while the engine is running.

sections.title: Scene · AI Demo / Estimating Engine
sections.body:
Add Scene “Engine Demo”. Sources → + → Display Capture (full screen). Add Audio Input Capture (your microphone). Press Start Recording before running the engine. Stop when done — the file lands in your configured recordings folder, then remux to MP4. Use this for parity run walkthroughs and portal demonstrations.

If Display Capture shows a black screen, that is the laptop’s hybrid graphics, not a broken install: use Window Capture on the specific window instead, or set OBS to the same GPU in Windows → Settings → Display → Graphics.

sections.title: Scene · Presentation (screen + face cam)
sections.body: Add Scene “Presentation”. Sources: Window Capture (select your slides or browser) + Video Capture Device (webcam) + Audio Input. Drag the webcam source to the bottom-right and resize it. Use for recording portal walkthroughs, AI tool demonstrations or client-facing demos.

sections.title: Scene · Facility Walkthrough
sections.body: Add Scene “Facility”. Sources: Video Capture Device (GoPro via USB, external camera or built-in laptop camera). Set output resolution to match your camera. Exports as MP4 for LinkedIn video, the SEEN newsletter or the wearesdi.com media library.

sections.title: Virtual Camera → Teams / Zoom / Meet
sections.body:
Start Virtual Camera is a button in the Controls dock, bottom-right of the main window, under Start Recording. In Teams: Settings → Devices → Camera → select OBS Virtual Camera. Everything in your active OBS scene broadcasts live into the call — switch scenes mid-call to share different layouts. Start the virtual camera before joining, or Teams may not list it.

Corrected 25 Aug 2026: this page previously said Tools → VirtualCam and told you to install the obs-virtualcam plugin. The virtual camera has been built into OBS on Windows since version 26.1 — the plugin is obsolete and installing it on a current OBS is more likely to break the feature than enable it.

sections.title: Streaming live · LinkedIn Live / YouTube
sections.body: Settings → Stream: select YouTube or Custom RTMP for LinkedIn Live. Paste your stream key from YouTube Studio or LinkedIn Live Events (you need to create the live event in advance on each platform to get the key). Press Start Streaming. OBS handles encoding; the platform handles distribution.

sections.title: Hotkeys worth setting
sections.body: Settings → Hotkeys. Recommended: Ctrl+Shift+R Start/Stop Recording, Ctrl+Shift+S Start/Stop Streaming, F1, F2… per scene. Hotkeys fire even when OBS is minimised — useful when the engine is running full-screen and you need to stop recording without switching windows.

inputs: Webcam or external camera (GoPro, USB cam)
Stream key for LinkedIn Live or YouTube
outputs: Virtual camera feed into Teams / Zoom / Meet
services.invoke: Launch OBS from the desktop. Select the right scene for the task, hit Start Recording or Start Streaming. Recordings land in your configured output folder (Settings → Output → Recording Path). Stop recording before closing the engine window.

services.name: SDI Tech Radar Intelligence

services.desc: Continuous intelligence scan of the global AI marketplace, tuned to SDI’s stack.
services.detail: A standing, evidence-based view of where AI is heading across SDI’s entire technology stack. Uses Claude Opus 4.8 with live web search to track the newest large language models, OCR and document-extraction engines, computer-vision systems, geometry and mathematical estimating models, 3D and generative-design tools, and simulation platforms including NVIDIA Omniverse and digital twins. Every run flags only what has changed since the last, giving the MD a true "what’s new" view. Runs on demand and can be scheduled weekly via Windows Task Scheduler.

ADOPT / TRIAL / ASSESS / HOLD rings per area
